subject.title: fix(shared): cap backtick delimiter length to prevent unbounded repeat

question: Where should OpenClaw bound pathological backtick input without allowing supplied content to escape its intended Markdown code container?
rationale: A fixed delimiter cap is unsafe, but choosing between upstream input rejection, a shared safe fallback, or retaining proportional delimiters defines a hostile-input and compatibility contract that automation should not invent.

options.title: Define a safe overflow policy
options.body: Preserve normal formatting, then reject oversized payloads or use a parser-proven fallback once a documented threshold is exceeded.

options.title: Keep proportional delimiters
options.body: Retain the current correctness invariant and accept output growth proportional to already-large input unless a concrete resource failure is reproduced.

options.title: Pause the hardening change
options.body: Close or defer this PR until a real resource-exhaustion path and a containment-safe mitigation are demonstrated.

recommendation.title: Define a safe overflow policy
recommendation.body: Preserve normal formatting, then reject oversized payloads or use a parser-proven fallback once a documented threshold is exceeded.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a shared-core security and compatibility contract rather than a mechanical constant adjustment.
